name: Iceland
headline: Iceland: +1.1% growth in 2025, 4.1% inflation, debt 57% of GDP
sections: Iceland is a $38.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 108th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.1% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $83K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.5% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.1% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 8.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.3% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 8.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 57% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 76% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −4.0% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 82% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −2.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 48% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.8 years (2024). Population: 389 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
